knowledge:
- key_parameters: drvr=Database driver ("SQLite" or "MariaDB") ;; asid=Assay source ID identifying the unique study name and phase ;; lvl=Processing level (0 for raw data, 1-6 for processed levels) ;; type=Data type, typically "mc" (multi-concentration) ;; slvl=Start level for data processing ;; elvl=End level for data processing ;; bline=Baseline margin type, e.g., "coff" (cutoff) or "bmad"
- alternatives: tcpl is the core package that GladiaTOX extends. GladiaTOX should be preferred when fetching raw image quantifications via web services, computing MECs based on historical data, exporting to ToxPI GUI, computing exposure severity scores, or requiring advanced QC reporting. MariaDB is recommended over SQLite for production environments and handling multiple studies.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for high-content screening (HCS) biomedical research data where multiple dose-response fittings, plate-level quality control, and standardized reporting are required.
- pitfalls: Failing to configure the database connection correctly using gtoxConf before running any operations ;; Assuming the default SQLite database is suitable for production (it is only for testing/vignettes; MariaDB should be used instead) ;; Attempting to fit dose-response models on series with fewer than 4 concentrations (minimum required for fitting) ;; Not computing the noise band (VMAD) before running higher-level processing (levels 4 to 6).

workflows.name: hcs_data_processing_and_reporting
workflows.intent: Process raw high-content screening (HCS) data and metadata through database loading, quality control, dose-response fitting, and comprehensive reporting.
input: plate_metadata.csv (plate metadata containing layout, wells, and endpoints)
raw_instrument_data.csv (image quantification raw data with measure values and plate IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Configure database connection ;; 2. Build assay table from plate and channel mapping metadata ;; 3. Register study info and load annotations into the database ;; 4. Prepare and write raw data to the database ;; 5. Assign default processing methods ;; 6. Run initial processing (levels 1-3) and compute the noise band (VMAD) ;; 7. Generate QC reports and mask low-quality plates ;; 8. Run full processing (levels 1-6) ;; 9. Generate final processing reports and plots
workflows.code:
sqlite_src <- file.path(system.file(package="GladiaTOX"), "sql",
                        "gladiatoxdb.sqlite")
gtoxConf(   drvr = "SQLite",
            host = NA,
            user = NA,
            pass = NULL,
            db = sqlite_src)
gtoxLoadAsid()
load(system.file("extdata", "data_for_vignette.rda", package="GladiaTOX"))
assay <- buildAssayTab(plate, chnmap)
std.nm <- "SampleStudy" # study name
phs.nm <- "PhaseII" # study phase
loadAnnot(plate, assay, NULL)
asid = gtoxLoadAsid(fld = c("asnm", "asph"), val = list(std.nm, phs.nm))$asid
dat <- prepareDatForDB(asid, dat)
gtoxWriteData(dat[ , list(acid, waid, wllq, rval)], lvl = 0, type = "mc")
assignDefaultMthds(asid = asid)
res <- gtoxRun(asid = asid, slvl = 1, elvl = 3, mc.cores = 2)
aeids <- gtoxLoadAeid(fld = "asid", val = asid)$aeid
tmp <- mapply(function(xx){
    tryCatch(gtoxCalcVmad(inputs = xx, aeid = xx, 
    notes = "computed within study"), 
    error = function(e) NULL)},
    as.integer(aeids))
res <- gtoxRun(asid = asid, slvl = 1, elvl = 6, mc.cores = 2)
gtoxReport(type = "qc", asid = asid, report_author = "report author",
report_title = "Vignette QC report", odir = outdir)
acnm <- "DNA damage (pH2AX)_DNA damage (pH2AX)_4h"
acid <- gtoxLoadAcid(fld=c("asid", "acnm"), val=list(asid,acnm))[, acid]
apid <- gtoxLoadApid()[u_boxtrack == "S-000031351", apid]
l2 <- gtoxLoadData(lvl = 2L, fld = "acid", val = acid)
gtoxPlotPlate(dat = l2, apid = apid, id = acid)
aeid <- gtoxLoadAeid(fld = c("acid", "analysis_direction"), 
                        val = list(acid, "up"))[, aeid]
spid <- gtoxLoadWaid(fld = c("apid", "wllt"), 
                        val = list(apid, "c"))[,unique(spid)]
m4id <- gtoxLoadData(lvl = 4L, fld = c("spid", "aeid"), 
                        val = list(spid, aeid))[, m4id]
gtoxPlotM4ID(m4id = m4id, lvl = 6, bline = "coff")
apid <- gtoxLoadApid()[u_boxtrack%in%"S-000030318", apid] # plate id
waids <- gtoxLoadWaid(fld="apid", val=apid)$waid #well ids
m0ids <- gtoxLoadData(lvl = 0, fld = "waid", val = waids)$m0id # raw data ids
gtoxSetWllq(ids = m0ids, wllq = 0, type = "mc") # set well quality to zero
res <- gtoxRun(asid = asid, slvl = 1, elvl = 6, mc.cores = 2)
gtoxReport(type = "all", asid = asid, report_author = "report author",
report_title = "Vignette Processing report", odir = outdir)
aeids <- gtoxLoadAeid(fld=c("asid", "aenm"),
val=list(asid, "DNA damage (pH2AX)_DNA damage (pH2AX)_24h_up"),
add.fld="asid")$aeid
m4id <- gtoxLoadData(lvl=4L)[(aeid==aeids & grepl("chromium", spid))]$m4id[1]
gtoxPlotM4ID(m4id = m4id, lvl = 6, bline = "coff")
chid <- gtoxLoadChem(field = "chnm", val = "chromium",
include.spid = FALSE)$chid
gtoxPlotWin(chid = chid, aeid = aeids, bline = "bmad", collapse = TRUE)
fname <- paste0(format(Sys.Date(), format="%y%m%d"), "_ASID", asid,"_MEC.pdf")
fname <- file.path(outdir, fname)
pdf(fname, width = 11, height = 7)
glPlotStat(asid)
dev.off()
chnms <- c("mercury", "o-cresol", "p-cresol")
glPlotPie(asid, chnms = chnms)
glPlotToxInd(asid)
